subject: GPU predictive-scaling runbook: on-prem throughput targets & failover
messages:

Subject: On-prem throughput target + planning request

Hi Kimberly,

We're getting close to production for our on-prem deployment and need a clearer throughput forecast and a concrete failover plan. Target: 180-220 requests/sec (avg request ~1.8k tokens, 95th token length ~3k) during daytime hours, spiky bursts to ~350 rps for short windows.

Can Redwood share recommended GPU counts + warm pool strategy, recommended headroom %, and a fallback model plan if we hit capacity? We also need an initial runbook for scaling events that we can hand to our infra team.

I've attached our Q1 workload CSV. Procurement may have follow-ups on SLA language later.

Thanks,
John

Subject: Re: On-prem throughput target + planning request

John — thanks, received the workload profile. Looping in Dev and Hiro to draft a predictive-scaling runbook and sizing notes.

Quick answers up-front:
- Approach: right-size steady-state for 220 rps and plan warm burst capacity for 350 rps with pre-warmed VMs + saved KV caches.
- Headroom: recommend 25% steady-state buffer (operational) and 1.5x short-burst capacity where latency SLO allows graceful degradation.
- Fallbacks: quantized model variant (8-bit) + lower context length cap as automatic fallback; route non-critical requests to a best-effort tier.

We'll produce a one-page runbook + a short set of playbook steps for your on-call. Expect draft tomorrow.

—Kimberly
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-29 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: internal: initial sizing calc + assumptions

Team — I pulled John's CSV and ran a quick throughput model. Assumptions: average generation cost = 0.9 GPU-seconds per 1k tokens on our optimized runtime; warm cache reduces token overhead by ~30% for repeated prefixes; target P95 latency <= 300ms for interactive tier.

Preliminary recommended steady-state (per DC):
- Baseline: 8 A100-like cards (logical equivalence) -> ~220 rps steady with 25% headroom.
- Burst pool: additional 6 pre-warmed cards (cold-starts avoided via VM warm pool + saved KV snapshots) to absorb short 350 rps windows for up to 5 minutes.
- If cost constrained: run with 6 baseline + 4 burst and rely on model-fallback at 300 rps.

Network/IO notes:
- KV cache checkpointing requires similar-sized local SSD and fast RDMA across nodes to keep eviction latency <8ms.
- Egress constraints: if external routing is used, we need <5ms intra-DC latency to meet P95 targets.

I attached a draft runbook (runbook-draft-v1.md) and a sample pcap we captured from their staging for reference.

- Dev
[attachment: runbook-draft-v1.md]

From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, John Ellis <john.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-29 12:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: initial sizing calc + assumptions

Agree with Dev. Two operational additions I want in the runbook:
1) Warm-pool lifecycle: minimum warm time 10 minutes; automated scale-in only after KV checkpoint success and <2% request load for 7 consecutive minutes.
2) Canary throttles: global token-bucket at the ingress that steps down to 60% for non-critical routes if node saturation >85%.

Failover options (order of preference):
A) Local burst pool (fastest)
B) Secondary DC within region (costly but preserves latency for many routes)
C) Fallback to quantized model instance (reduces throughput pressure, increases per-request CPU usage)

I'll add these to the runbook. Also: recommend a synthetic workload job that runs every 2 minutes to validate end-to-end latency and warm cache health.

—Hiro

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-30 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: runbook + ops checklist draft attached

Attached is a cleaned runbook and a short ops checklist after incorporating Dev/Hiro notes. Highlights:
- SLA triggers: warn at 70% steady-state utilization; scale-up automation kicks at 80%; manual escalation thresholds at 90%.
- Observability: track tokens/sec, GPU utilization per-card, queue depth, KV miss rate, tail latency (P99), and synthetic-test success ratio.
- Playbook steps for scale event (short):
  1) Confirm synthetic job failure and KV miss spike.
  2) Enable burst-pool via autoscaler (pre-warmed VMs).
  3) If utilization remains >85% after 90s, trigger cross-DC failover to secondary.
  4) If cross-DC not available, flip non-critical routes to quantized model.

I've attached network pcap samples for their infra team.

[attachment: network-latency-sample.pcap]

Please review — if John approves, we'll finalize and hand over to Acme's infra by EOD tomorrow.

—Evelyn

John — attaching the finalized runbook and checklist (incorporates headroom, warm-pool lifecycle, autoscaler thresholds and failover order). The key commitments here:
- Steady-state recommendation: 8 GPUs per DC with 25% buffer.
- Short-burst capacity: +6 pre-warmed GPUs to cover 350 rps spikes up to 5 minutes.
- Observable KPIs and automated thresholds as listed.

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm whether you want secondary DC failover (we can help configure) — this adds cost but preserves latency.
2) Sign off on fallback order (quantized model + route-level throttling).
3) Procurement: we included a simple SLA addendum around warm-pool availability; please confirm any redlines.

If you sign off, we'll schedule a 60-minute knowledge transfer with your infra team next week and provide the runbook as a runbook-as-code repo.
